strings.name: Dario Amodei
strings.summary: Amodei moved from physics and neuroscience into deep learning, working at Google Brain and OpenAI before co-founding Anthropic with Daniela Amodei and others. He helped develop the Claude model family and research on interpretability, reliability and human feedback. His influence spans frontier-model competition and AI safety debate. The company's safety goals and his forecasts must be distinguished from demonstrated technical achievements.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 2026-11-13; selected public career milestones extend to January 2026. Forecasts and policy arguments in his essays are not treated as events that have already occurred.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Physics degree at Stanford; physics PhD at Princeton, researching biophysics
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Associated organizations
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Claude and research organization
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Co-founded Anthropic and helped develop the Claude conversational model family and products for users and developers.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: AI safety and interpretability
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Worked on safety research at OpenAI and Anthropic, including human preferences, model reliability and understanding internal mechanisms.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Publishes an essay on AI risks
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The Adolescence of Technology discusses possible risks to security, economies and democracy; these are his analyses and arguments.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Anthropic introduces Claude
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The company released a conversational assistant for partners and developers, entering the generative AI application market.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Co-founds Anthropic
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Established the company with Daniela Amodei and other partners, emphasizing reliability, interpretability and safety research.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Joins OpenAI
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Later became vice president of research, contributing to GPT-2, GPT-3 and long-term safety research.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Completes Princeton doctorate
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Completed research on neural-circuit electrophysiology, then undertook postdoctoral research at Stanford Medicine.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Receives Hertz Fellowship
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Received the fellowship while pursuing physics and biophysics research at Princeton.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Born in San Francisco
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Born in the United States; later studied physics at Stanford University.
